prompt: A wave is described by $y = 3\sin(x) + 2$. What is the largest value $y$ ever reaches?
hint: $\sin(x)$ never climbs above $1$, no matter what $x$ is.

hints.text: $\sin(x)$ never climbs above $1$, no matter what $x$ is.
Put the biggest possible value in: $3 \times 1 + 2$.

explanation: The plain sine wave swings between $-1$ and $1$.
Multiplying by $3$ stretches that swing to between $-3$ and $3$ — that is the amplitude.
Adding $2$ lifts the whole wave up by $2$, so the top is $3 + 2 = 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Midline plus amplitude
steps: The $+2$ sets the midline at $y = 2$ — the level the wave rocks around.
The amplitude $3$ says it rises $3$ above that line and falls $3$ below.
